newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK police to handle handover security without China.
newsitem.headline: HK police to handle handover security without China.

text.p: Hong Kong police said on Wednesday they were talking with China's Public Security Bureau (PSB) about the territory's handover in June, but that no mainland officers would be involved in security arrangements.
"We have been advising them in general terms on our plans for the handover and listening to their views," Dick Lee, Assistant Commissioner of Police (Special Duties), told a news conference.
"As far as the security arrangements for the handover ceremonies, it is the sole responsibility of the Hong Kong police force."

Lee, who heads a team responsible for security at the lavish celebrations and ceremonies planned for the handover, said more than 2,000 police would be assigned to protect dignitaries and other visitors as well as to oversee the official events.

Police will have their hands full as Hong Kong is bracing for a flood of tourists, journalists and official guests to witness the British territory's historic transition to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.
Colonial Governor Chris Patten, Chinese officials and hundreds of invited guests will bring the curtain down on the handover events with a ceremony at the harbour-side Convention Centre.
"Our force has no experience in handling these types of events," Lee said.
The team had been preparing by visiting international conferences in Madrid, Washington and Singapore as well as the Olympic Games in Atlanta, Lee said.
Two groups are scheduled to visit Beijing over the next two weeks as guests of the PSB to observe security measures and traffic control at two large events there.
Lee's team will also oversee security at a joint meeting of the World Bank and International Monetary Fund in Hong Kong in September.
